Top 30 Best Private School in England
At Windrush Valley Prep School Oxfordshire, we believe that every child deserves the best possible start.
Our classes, averaging 14 pupils, provide personalised attention, ensuring the highest education standards. Focused on nurturing self-esteem, confidence, and independence, we prepare boys and girls aged 3-11 for success in independent or state senior schools. Over the past 25 years, all our pupils passed the senior school entry exam and joined their chosen secondary schools.
Our Nursery
At Windrush Valley School Nursery, we give children more than a great start – we nurture a lifelong love of learning. In a warm, supportive environment, curiosity is celebrated, confidence grows, and every child is truly known. Visit Our Nursery section for more details.
Best Prep School Oxfordshire
The school is ranked in the top 30 independent preparatory schools in England by the Sunday Times. Earning it the prestigious accolade of Best Prep School Oxfordshire. The school has also received an Award for Excellence by the Independent School Association. Small class sizes, highly experience teaching staff, affordable fees, and a focus on academic excellence are the fundamental tenets of the school.
Exceptional Education, Sensible Fees – from £3,200 per term
We understand that choosing the right education for your child is a significant investment. As a school consistently ranked among the Top 30 Best Private Schools in England, we are deeply committed to providing an exceptional learning environment that nurtures each child’s potential. We believe that this high-quality education should be accessible to as many families as possible, which is why we strive to maintain a transparent and sensible school fees structure.
We recognise the current economic climate and the impact of VAT on school fees. This makes our commitment to providing outstanding value for your investment even more critical. Our fees start from £3,200 (ex VAT) per term.

Employers Childcare Voucher Scheme
Employers Childcare Voucher Scheme
A Childcare Voucher Scheme provides savings for employers and employees, making it a popular, cost effective childcare payment scheme. As a parent, you simply swap part of your salary (salary sacrifice) for childcare vouchers. The amount sacrificed is exempt from tax and National Insurance Contributions. It is a cost effective way of paying for additional nursery and childcare fees. The government set the criteria and therefore, rules for qualification do change from time to time. Therefore, you should review relevant government websites and other resources to see the current rules and eligibility.
Using your childcare vouchers at Windrush Valley Prep School Oxfordshire
We support the use of vouchers from several company providers. If you would like to use vouchers toward your additional nursery or childcare fees at Windrush Valley Prep School Oxfordshire , and your company provider is not listed below, please contact the school office with your company details and childcare voucher provider. We will complete the school registration process for you and provide you with a registration number to enable you to claim your vouchers through your company. We are always happy to help where we can. The school is currently registered for childcare vouchers with the following providers:
If you would like more details about the scheme and how we can help, please feel free to contact us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Enrichment Week - Windrush Valley Prep School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Enrichment Week
Curriculum enrichment week
Each year, Windrush Valley Preparatory School Oxfordshire organises a Curriculum Enrichment Week to encourage children to “think outside of the box”. The children are given an opportunity to study a themed topic outside the school’s regular curriculum.
A fun week packed with activities and events is delivered, more often than not, outside the usual classroom environment and with different teachers. Groups involving children from across the age range are formed to allow older and younger children to study together. After they have concluded their studies, the week culminates with a whole school presentation of the work produced during the week. During these presentations we encourage every team member to take a part in presenting their studies.
The week seeks to encourage a passion for self-learning as well as providing valuable experience of working with others to achieve a desired goal. In addition, the older children within the groupings are encouraged to take a leadership role and to learn our working together benefits all. These types of activities, along with others that we run throughout the year at the school, also help to build self-esteem and confidence. This is just one of the numerous activities we run at the school that not only develops our pupil’s academic excellence but also their behavioural and social excellence too.
The pupils are initially guided by the teachers in terms of subject matters that will be covered. After this initial guidance it is up to the children to reach a consensus within their teams on who will study and research the particular aspects of the subject. Themes are varied with topics that include science, art, music, literature, history, geography, technology and social studies. Pupils are also encouraged to think about new ways to present their findings to others. Ways that educate and create interest.
Windrush Valley Preparatory Oxfordshire has an outstanding track record of performance, education and the enjoyment of school life experienced by our pupils. For more information about our school and our planning of our pupil’s education, activities and social development, please click the following link: Private Prep School Oxfordshire.
In addition to the Curriculum Enrichment Week, the school arranges two residential trips per year: a 3 day activity in the United Kingdom for Year 6 during their last term at school, and a week either abroad or in the UK for Year 4, Year 5, and Year 6 early in the new academic year. Previous trips have included visiting Holland, France, York and Edinburgh. Residential and adventure trips enable children to develop self-esteem and confidence and enjoy different cultures and languages – further enriching the curriculum and the children’s life-experience.

pageCache.pageTitle: Windrush Valley Prep School Oxfordshire - Performing Arts
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
Windrush Valley Prep School Oxfordshire – Performing Arts
Windrush Valley Prep School Oxfordshire has a rich heritage in the performing arts. Drama, music, and public speaking are one of the foundational elements of building self-esteem, self-confidence, and creative expression.
School productions
Our annual school productions are universally recognised for their high standard of production and performance. Young children begin their acting career with the traditional nativity in the local church, supported by the cast of the whole school. As well as performing, children are regulatory involved in the production of stage props and back-stage logistics. Older children in Year 3 and above enjoy performing in a full stage production each Easter in a major whole school production of a popular musical. In addition to school productions, all pupils regularly play in the school band, perform in musicals on stage, compete in public speaking competitions and sing in the choir.
Music
All children have the opportunity to learn to play at least one musical instrument of choice and have the opportunity to play in the school band. By the time children leave school they will have achieved good grades in the Royal School for Music examinations, sometimes with more than one instrument. Musical instrument lessons are available in wind, brass, piano and percussion. The Chipping Norton Music Festival is an annual, week long, celebration of local musical and artistic talent. Each year the Windrush Valley Private School Oxfordshire band receives high acclaim from the Festival judges for the high quality of its performance. Individual children demonstrate their skill and artistry in the poetry and reading sections and our choir always ‘sings its socks off’ to the audience’s obvious delight.
English Speaking Board (ESB)
Each year children from Year 2 upwards are entered for the prestigious ESB competitions. Pupils recite a poem from memory, read a passage from a favourite book and prepare a talk on a topic of personal interest. Additionally, all children have to demonstrate their ability to listen to each other’s presentation and ask sensible and pertinent questions at the end. Each year children from Windrush Valley Private School Oxfordshire receive well deserved high praise and marks for their performances.

HEADTEACHER WELCOME
Mrs Lucy Maudsley BEd (Hons), Headteacher
Welcome to Windrush Valley Prep School and Nursery.
It is a privilege to welcome you to Windrush Valley Prep School and Nursery, a small and nurturing independent school where every child is known, valued and encouraged to thrive.
From Nursery to Year 6, we provide a broad and ambitious education that combines strong academic foundations with creativity, sport, outdoor learning and enriching experiences. Our small classes allow us to understand each child as an individual, providing the right balance of support and challenge so that they develop confidence, independence and a genuine love of learning.
Our approach is rooted in the values of effort, kindness and responsibility. We want our pupils to achieve their best academically while also growing into thoughtful, resilient and compassionate young people. Through our curriculum, pastoral care and distinctive WINDRUSH360 and WAVES360 programmes, children are encouraged to explore their interests, embrace new opportunities and develop the practical skills and strength of character they will need for the future.
Windrush Valley Prep School and Nursery is a warm, happy and inclusive community in which positive relationships sit at the heart of school life. We work closely with families to ensure that every child feels secure, inspired and ready to take their next steps with confidence.
I warmly invite you to visit us and discover what makes Windrush Valley Prep School and Nursery such a special place to learn and grow.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Parents’ Consultative Group - Windrush Valley Prep School
pageCache.text:
The Parents’ Consultative Group
The Parents’ Consultative Group
The Parents’ Consultative Group (PCG) is unique to Windrush Valley Prep School Oxfordshire (ISI 2010). The group is comprised of three separate committees, all working together to support every pupil and the school community as a whole.
The Parent Representative Committee
Each class has a parent representative who liaises between the class parents/carers and the school. They network with their class parents and the other class representatives. Their role is to signpost parents/carers to the correct support within school, share reminders or raise questions on behalf of the class.
The Enrichment Committee
This is a group who work together to further enhance the many enrichment opportunities at the school. These opportunities may include guest speakers, co-curricular clubs, local or national initiatives, to name just a few. The committee source the support, skills and expertise of parents and the wider community to bring an extensive range and breadth of experiences to the school.
The Social Committee
This group helps to organise social events for the children, parents and families. The events are often run as a fundraising event as well as an opportunity for the school community to join together. These events include: school discos, quiz nights, movie nights, the summer family social and many more social gatherings.
We encourage all parents to be part of the PCG as we recognise the importance of the school developing strong home-school links. Such partnerships and collaboration bring a wealth of support and shared skills and interests to both the individual child and the school community as a whole.

pageCache.pageTitle: Windrush Valley Private School Oxfordshire - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
At Windrush Valley Private School, we are dedicated to providing an excellent start to every child’s educational journey. Our diverse and comprehensive curriculum is designed to foster individual growth, ensuring each child receives personalised attention within our small class sizes, averaging around 14 pupils. Many of our devoted teachers have been with the school for several years, ensuring stability, continuity, and a wealth of experience all tailored for our pupil’s growth and success.
Curriculum Principles:

A Day in Our Nursery – Through a Child’s Eyes
by admin | May 3, 2026 | Nursery
Drop-off at Windrush Valley Prep School & Nursery starts the way every good day should – with a warm welcome. Coats are hung on pegs, shoes are swapped for wellies if it has been raining, and within moments, the children are settled and ready to explore.
But what does a typical nursery day actually look like? Here is a glimpse through the eyes of the children who spend their days with us.
Morning – Discovering and Doing
The morning begins with free-flow play, where children choose from carefully set-up activities. One child heads straight for the water tray. Another is building a tower with wooden blocks, counting as she goes. A small group gathers at the craft table to paint butterflies.
This is not random play. Pouring water develops fine motor control. Counting blocks introduces early maths. Mixing paint teaches cause and effect. Our Early Years team set up these invitations to learn based on each child’s interests and next steps.
Later in the morning, we gather on the carpet for phonics. Songs, stories, and sound games bring letters to life. With an average class size of just 14 pupils, every child gets their moment – answering a question, holding up a letter card, or leading the group in a favourite rhyme.
Outside – Whatever the Weather
Our nursery children spend a generous part of each day outdoors. Set in the Cotswolds village of Ascott-under-Wychwood, we have beautiful grounds and we make the most of them.
On a sunny day, you will find children digging in the mud kitchen, riding balance bikes, or hunting for minibeasts in the garden. During Forest School sessions, they learn to take measured risks – balancing on logs, building dens, and exploring nature first-hand.
Afternoon – Winding Down, Not Switching Off
After lunch and a rest, the afternoon has a gentler pace. There might be a cooking activity, a group story on the carpet, or a chance to return to a favourite activity from the morning.
By the time parents arrive for pick-up, children have had a full, purposeful day. They have practised sharing, tried something new, and spent time outdoors – known and cared for by adults who understand them.
More Than Childcare
At Windrush Valley Prep School & Nursery, our nursery is not simply childcare – it is the start of a child’s education. With 97% of our Early Years children achieving a Good Level of Development, the foundations we lay here matter.
We keep things small because small works. Small enough to notice when a child is ready for their next challenge. Small enough to celebrate every milestone. Small enough to truly know every child.
Come and see for yourself. We welcome prospective families to visit, meet our team, and experience nursery life first-hand. Book a visit or call us on 01993 831793.

Windrush Valley School Nursery: Where Curious Minds Begin
by admin | Feb 15, 2026 | Nursery
Windrush Valley School Nursery: Where Curious Minds Begin
At Windrush Valley School Nursery, we give children more than a great start – we nurture a lifelong love of learning. In a warm, supportive environment, curiosity is celebrated, confidence grows, and every child is truly known. Our engaging Early Years curriculum inspires independence, resilience, and the social skills that set children up for future success.
Guided by the belief that “play is the highest form of research,” we blend purposeful play with structured learning. Children thrive academically, socially, and emotionally, developing kindness, confidence, and the strong character that defines a Windrush Valley pupil.
We welcome children from the term after their third birthday. Through all seven areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage, learning comes alive with play-based exploration, early phonics, and number work – creating happy, confident learners eager to explore the world.
Discover Our Wondertots Sessions
Each half-term, families are invited to Wondertots – a relaxed morning session in our nursery. Explore the environment, meet our caring team, and experience the joy of learning in action. It’s the perfect introduction to our nurturing community.
Flexible Childcare Options
All 3- and 4-year-olds are entitled to 15 funded hours per week, with eligible families able to access up to 30 hours.
Day Nursery – Session Times:
Morning: 09:00–12:00Afternoon: 12:00–15:00Full Day: 09:00–15:00
Additional sessions and wrap-around care are available, including before school (08:00–09:00) and after school care (up to 18:00).
Healthy Meals
We offer nutritious meals and packed options with dietary needs fully supported.
A Confident Start to School Life
A settling-in taster session helps every child feel secure and excited from day one. As the natural gateway to Windrush Valley School, our nursery provides a seamless transition into Reception class and beyond.
Contact us
Discover how your child can flourish at Windrush Valley School Day Nursery. Contact our Admissions Registrar to arrange a visit or learn more about joining our community.

pageCache.pageTitle: FAQ - Windrush Valley Prep School Oxfordshire
pageCache.text:
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
About the School
1. Where is Windrush Valley School located?
Windrush Valley School is set in the heart of the Cotswolds village of Ascott-under-Wychwood, near Chipping Norton, Oxfordshire (postcode OX7 6AN). The school is easily accessible from across West Oxfordshire, the Evenlode Valley, and the wider Cotswolds, with families joining from towns and villages including Burford, Witney, Woodstock, and Charlbury.
2. What age range does Windrush Valley School cater for?
Windrush Valley School welcomes boys and girls from the term after they turn 3 through to Year 6 (age 11), offering a carefully structured and continuous educational journey from Nursery to the end of the prep school years.
3. What are the latest inspection results for Windrush Valley School?
Windrush Valley School is inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) and is registered with the Department for Education, the Independent Schools Council (ISC), and the Independent Schools Association (ISA). The school’s most recent inspection report is available on the ISI website. Windrush Valley was also recognised by the Sunday Times as one of the Top 30 independent preparatory schools in England.
Admissions & Entry
4. What is the admissions process at Windrush Valley School?
The process begins with an initial enquiry and a visit to the school, during which prospective families meet with senior staff and see the school in action. Children take part in age-appropriate assessments or taster sessions as part of the process. The admissions team is happy to guide families through each step.
5. Are mid-year admissions possible?
Yes. Where places are available, Windrush Valley School is happy to consider mid-year or non-standard entry points. The school works closely with families to ensure a smooth transition at any stage.
6. Is there a waiting list?
Some year groups may have waiting lists due to the school’s intentionally small class sizes. Early application is encouraged, and the admissions team will keep families informed of availability.
7. How do I arrange a visit or attend an open day?
Prospective families are warmly welcome to visit the school. Open day dates are published on the school website, and private tours can be arranged at any time by contacting the school office on 01993 831793 or via the enquiry form on the website. Visits offer the chance to meet staff, see lessons in progress, and get a feel for the school’s community and ethos.
Teaching, Learning & Progress
8. What curriculum does Windrush Valley School follow?
The school delivers a broad and balanced curriculum aligned with national expectations, enriched by specialist teaching, creativity, and cross-curricular learning. Subjects include English, mathematics, science, history, geography, French, art, music, drama, PE, and computing. The curriculum is designed to develop a genuine love of learning, and pupils achieve well and make strong progress across all year groups.
9. What curriculum does the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) follow?
Children in the EYFS learn through a carefully planned, topic-based approach that covers both the prime and specific areas of learning. The school uses Jolly Phonics as its synthetic phonics programme, and alongside this, children develop strong reading comprehension skills from an early stage. There is a purposeful balance between adult-led activities and child-initiated play, giving children plenty of opportunities to explore, investigate, and build confidence in a nurturing setting.
10. How does Windrush Valley School prepare pupils for senior schools?
The school combines strong academic foundations with an emphasis on independence, confidence, curiosity, and the broader learning skills needed for a successful transition to senior school. Pupils are well prepared for entry to both independent and state secondary schools. The school has a strong track record of pupils securing places and scholarships at leading senior schools across the region.
11. What are the class sizes at Windrush Valley School?
Class sizes are intentionally small, typically between 12 and 14 pupils. This allows teachers to know each child as an individual and to provide highly personalised support, challenge, and feedback. Small class sizes are one of the school’s defining strengths and a key reason families choose Windrush Valley.
12. How does the school support children of different abilities?
Teaching is carefully differentiated to stretch more able pupils while providing targeted support for those who need it. The school’s small class sizes mean that teachers can closely monitor each child’s progress and adapt their approach to ensure every pupil is appropriately challenged and supported.
13. How does Windrush Valley School extend and challenge more able pupils?
Extension and enrichment are embedded within everyday lessons and further developed through clubs, projects, competitions, and individual challenges. The school’s approach ensures that the most able pupils are consistently stretched and motivated to achieve their best.
14. How is progress assessed and monitored?
Progress is tracked through ongoing observation, formative assessments, and regular reviews, ensuring that teaching responds to each child’s individual needs. The school uses a combination of continuous assessment and more formal benchmarks to measure attainment and identify areas for further development.
15. How is progress shared with parents?
Parents receive written reports at the end of the autumn and summer terms, and attend two parent–teacher meetings each year. Beyond this, staff are readily available for informal conversations, and the school maintains open, ongoing communication with families throughout the year.
Pastoral Care & Wellbeing
16. What pastoral care does Windrush Valley School provide?
Pastoral care is a high priority at Windrush Valley School, and what is best for each pupil is at the heart of every decision. The school’s Windrush360 programme is designed to develop the whole child – academically, socially, emotionally, and physically – rather than focusing solely on academic achievement. As a result, the school is a positive, happy place where children feel safe, valued, and eager to learn.
17. How well do staff know the children?
Very well. The combination of small class sizes and a close-knit school community means that every member of staff knows every child by name. Strong staff–pupil relationships are central to the school’s ethos, and every child is known individually, valued, and supported both academically and personally.
18. How does Windrush Valley School support children with Special Educational Needs (SEN)?
The school offers dedicated SEN support and works closely with parents and, where appropriate, external specialists to ensure that each child’s individual needs are met. Support is tailored to the child, and the school’s small class sizes allow for close monitoring and early intervention when needed.
19. What is the school’s approach to behaviour and discipline?
The Windrush360 programme sets clear expectations and motivates pupils to do their best, both in lessons and during less structured times of the day. Pupils are friendly and welcoming, and routinely display good manners and respect for others. The school’s approach emphasises positive reinforcement and personal responsibility.
20. How does Windrush Valley School handle bullying?
The school has a clear anti-bullying policy and takes a proactive, prompt, and sensitive approach to any concerns, working in close partnership with parents. Pupils learn about bullying through the curriculum – including what it is, how to recognise it, and what to do if they experience or witness it. The school’s small, close community means that issues are identified and addressed quickly.
21. How are new pupils supported when they join the school?
Transition into the school is carefully planned and supported. New pupils are paired with a buddy, receive dedicated classroom support during their first weeks, and benefit from close communication between the school and their family. The school’s warm, welcoming community helps new children settle in quickly and confidently.
Enrichment & School Life
22. What extracurricular activities are available at Windrush Valley School?
Pupils enjoy a wide range of clubs and activities, including sport, music, drama, academic enrichment, and creative arts. After-school clubs run until 16:30 for children in Years 1–6 and are included in the school fees at no additional cost. The programme changes termly to give children the opportunity to try new activities and discover new interests.
23. What role does outdoor learning play at the school?
Outdoor learning is central to Windrush Valley School’s ethos, supporting physical wellbeing, teamwork, confidence, and creativity. The school’s beautiful Cotswolds setting provides an ideal environment for learning beyond the classroom. Timetabled Forest School sessions are available for children in Nursery through to Year 2, and outdoor activities and exploration are woven into the wider curriculum across all year groups.
24. Are school trips and residential experiences offered?
Yes. The school organises a range of age-appropriate trips and enrichment visits throughout the year, linked to the curriculum and designed to bring learning to life. Residential trips are offered to older pupils, helping to develop independence, resilience, and social skills in a supportive setting.
Practical Information & Community
25. What are the school hours and term dates?
Core school hours are 08:50 to 15:30. After-school clubs run until 16:30 and are included in the fees for children in Years 1–6. Term dates are published annually and shared well in advance with families via the school website and ParentMail.
26. Is wraparound care available at Windrush Valley School?
Yes. The school is open from 08:00 until 18:00, providing wraparound care before and after the school day. This extended provision is designed to support busy families while ensuring children are in a safe, familiar, and enriching environment throughout.
27. What do school fees include?
Fees are clearly structured and include tuition, core educational activities, and after-school clubs. Windrush Valley School is committed to providing affordable educational excellence, and full details of the current fee schedule are available from the admissions team or on the school website. The school also offers sibling discounts.
28. Does Windrush Valley School offer scholarships or bursaries?
Families interested in financial assistance are encouraged to contact the school directly to discuss their circumstances. The school is committed to accessibility and will work with families wherever possible. Details of any available bursary support can be obtained from the admissions team.
29. How does the school communicate with parents?
The school’s primary communication channel is ParentMail, which is used for newsletters, updates, and day-to-day information. Parents also receive written reports twice a year, attend two parent–teacher meetings annually, and benefit from ongoing, informal communication with staff. The school values open and responsive communication with all families.
30. How involved can parents be in school life?
Parents are valued partners in the school community. Families are encouraged to join the Parents Consultative Group (PCG) and to engage through a range of events, workshops, and celebrations throughout the year. The school actively welcomes parent involvement and sees it as an important part of each child’s education.
31. What senior schools do Windrush Valley pupils go on to?
Windrush Valley School has a strong record of preparing pupils for entry to a wide range of senior schools, both independent and state. Pupils regularly secure places at leading schools across Oxfordshire and beyond, and the school is proud of its track record of scholarship awards. The admissions team is happy to share recent destination data with prospective families on request.

Nursery Fees & Funded Hours
Windrush Valley School – Nursery Fees & Funded Hours
At Windrush Valley School Nursery, we believe an exceptional early education should be within reach of every family. Our nursery fees are simple, transparent and sensibly priced, with all 3 and 4-year-olds entitled to 15 funded hours per week through Local Authority funding – and eligible families able to access up to 30 hours. With part-time, full-time and extended day options from 08:00 to 18:00, you only pay for the childcare you need, while your child enjoys the warm, nurturing start that sees 97% of our Early Years children attain a Good Level of Development (GLD) – far surpassing both national and local results. To put this into context, the Department for Education has set a national target at 75%. The most recent national figure currently stands at 67.7%. Within the Oxfordshire the level is 69%.
Understanding Your Funding
All children aged 3 and 4 are entitled to 15 hours of funded education and childcare per week with an additional 15 hours for working parents who meet the eligibility criteria. You can check your eligibility here: https://www.gov.uk/free-childcare-if-working/check-youre-eligible.
1 September – 31 December
1 January – 31 March
Making The Most of Your Funding
Attendance for pupils with 15 funded hours can be used in a variety of combinations either for a morning, afternoon or full day – to make up 5 sessions. Attendance for pupils with 30 funded hours covers up to 10 sessions
Enhancing Your Child’s Nursery Experience
We offer a range of optional extras to enhance your child’s week and simplify your routine.
Non-funded sessions
Ad hoc sessions
Forest School enrichment
Wrap Around Care
Additional Childcare
Creative consumables
Non-Funded Sessions
Research shows that children who gradually increase their nursery hours transition more smoothly to full-time school. We recommend considering additional sessions throughout the year so your child is comfortably attending at least 4 days by the summer term. This will ensure that they are better equipped and prepared for the increase to 5 full days per week along with the increased pace of learning required in the Reception class.
Autumn Term(14 weeks)
Spring Term(10 weeks)
Summer term(11 weeks)

Note: Secure your preferred schedule early as availability is limited
For part time pupils, we recommended the following patterns of attendance:
Invoices for non-funded sessions are sent out at the end of the preceding term and are payable by the start of the new term.
Autumn: 2-3 days/week “settle in”
Spring: 3-4 days/week “build confidence”
Summer: 4-5 days/week “Reception ready”
Ad hoc Sessions
Last minute ad hoc sessions charged at £35 per session, can be booked (subject to availability).
Forest School Enrichment
As part of our enriching curriculum, we offer off-site Forest School sessions. If your child attends on a Forest School Day, a termly fee of £70 applies. These sessions are designed to build resilience, creativity, and confidence through outdoor exploration.
If you prefer not to participate, your child will engage in alternative EYFS activities at school.
Wrap Around Care
Windrush Valley School Nursey provides flexible care options. Daily options include:
Before School Care (BSC)
Drop off any time between 08:00-09:00 – No pre-booking needed
After School Care (ASC)
Charged in 30-minute increments – Booked on a weekly basis
After 18:00 Mon-Thu; after 15:30 Fri
Specific educational needs will normally be defined as having an EHCP or specific diagnosis from an outside professional that determines the need for targeted intervention but can include pupils requiring Specialist Support in Phase 3 without an EHCP or specific diagnosis.
The above charges will be invoiced retrospectively at the end of each term. We also accept childcare vouchers for payment of wrap around care.
After School Care bundles provide supervised care after the core sessions, includes tea, and offers the best available value.

Additional Childcare
Stay and Play Days: Windrush Valley School Nursery runs two additional days at the end of each half term where children can enjoy seasonal crafts, games and a movie.
Activity weeks: One additional week is provided at the end of the Autumn and Spring terms and two weeks at the end of the Summer Term. These weeks provide more structured play and sessions including Cotswold Stage School and sports activities.
Children can attend one or more days as needed. These are charged at £55 per day at the time of booking. We also accept childcare vouchers for payment for this additional childcare.
Creative Consumables
Children enjoy daily access to a wide variety of creative materials as part of our core EYFS curriculum at no additional cost. Occasionally, we offer special creative projects using materials like clay or individual craft kits – which allow children to explore new skills and materials. You will be notified in advance of any small cost for these projects.
If you choose not to participate, your child will take part in an alternative EYFS-approved activity.
School Meals
The school offers chef-prepared options that save time and ensure balanced nutrition:
Children attending full days and afternoon sessions have a choice of a hot school meal (£4.50) or a packed lunch (£4.00). Packed lunches are also available for morning-session only children to take home. A Packed Tea is available for those wishing to take one home at 15:00 or when staying for After School Care.
Packed Lunch/Tea provide a well-balanced meal with varied choices that include a selection of bread and fillings, vegetable pots, cheeses, fruit, cookie/cake/yogurt and a drink. Gluten free and dairy free options are available.
For more information, please view our nursery page and nursery admissions page.

Nursery Life
Nursery Life
From the moment your child arrives to the moment they leave, every part of the Nursery day is designed with purpose, warmth, and care. Here is a snapshot about how life works in our Nursery.
The Nursery Day
The school is open from 08:00 to 18:00, Mon to Thurs, and from 08:00 to 15:30 on Fridays. Our core Nursery funded sessions run as follows:
Flexible Childcare That Works For You
We offer a range of flexible options designed to fit around your family’s needs – from government-funded sessions to wrap-around care and holiday programmes.
Government Funded Nursery Places
Children aged 3 & 4 are entitled to 15 funded hours per week. Working parents who meet the eligibility can access 30 funded hours. Funding applies to core sessions between 09:00 and 15:00.
Before School Care from 08:00 every morning — no pre-booking needed. After School Care runs 15:00–18:00, Monday to Thursday, bookable weekly or as a discounted termly bundle.
Build attendance gradually: 2–3 days in autumn to settle in, 3–4 in spring to build confidence, and 4–5 in summer to be Reception-ready. Ad hoc sessions also available at short notice.
Stay & Play + Activity Weeks
End-of-half-term Stay and Play days with crafts, games, and films. End-of-term Activity Weeks with Cotswold Stage School and sports sessions. Childcare vouchers accepted.
A Typical Week – Nursery Life
Every week in our Nursery includes a rich blend of adult-led teaching and child-initiated exploration.
Outdoor exploration & nature
Phonics, maths & creative play
Stories, songs & exploration
PE, teamwork & confidence
Arts and creativity learning
Throughout the week, children also enjoy whole-school assemblies at Holy Trinity Church, story time, outdoor play in the garden, and plenty of time for imaginative, child-led exploration. More information is available by visiting Our Nursery page.
Meals and Snacks
Good nutrition supports good learning. All children bring a healthy snack for morning break – ideally fruit-based. For lunch, families can choose from three options:
Chef-prepared on site by our catering partner Apetito, offering balanced, seasonal menus.
A well-balanced selection of sandwiches, vegetables, cheese, fruit. Gluten-free and dairy-free available.
Packed Lunch from Home
If preferred, families are more than welcome to provide their child's own lunch each day.
Nursery Admissions
Visit our Nursery Admissions page or complete the form below to book your Nursery visit or request more information.

pageCache.pageTitle: Windrush Valley School Nursery - Our Nursery
pageCache.text:
Windrush Valley School Nursery
An inspiring, nurturing, and high-achieving start for children aged 3 to 4, delivered by one of the top 30 private schools in England and the highest-ranked in Oxfordshire.
At Windrush Valley School Nursery, we give children more than a great start – we nurture a lifelong love of learning. In a warm, supportive environment, curiosity is celebrated, confidence grows, and every child is truly known. Our engaging Early Years curriculum inspires independence, resilience, and the social skills that set children up for future success.
Giving your child the best possible start
Affordable Pricing
Exceptional learning environment with sensible fees, including Local Authority funding.
Complete Flexibility
Part-time and full-time Nursery places available, including extended day options.
Continuity & Comfort
The best possible start to your child’s schooling – with seamless integration into school life.
Flexible Childcare Options
All 3 and 4-year-olds are entitled to 15 funded hours per week, with eligible families able to access up to 30 hours.
Session Times:
Morning: 09:00–12:00Afternoon: 12:00–15:00Full Day: 09:00–15:00
Additional sessions and wrap-around care are available, including before school (08:00–09:00) and after school care (up to 18:00).
Nursery Life
From the moment your child arrives to the moment they leave, every part of the Nursery day is designed with purpose, warmth, and care. Find out more about Nursery Life and flexible childcare options.
‘Wondertots’
Wondertots is our half termly stay and play sessions for ages 2-3 year olds. Wondertots is completely free of charge and is open to all families in the community. Children do not need to be enrolled in our Nursery to attend – everyone is welcome. Please complete the contact form below for more details.
“We think the school is doing an amazing job, providing an environment that the children totally enjoy and thrive in.”
Latest inspection - comments:
“The curriculum is carefully designed to cover a breadth of learning in ways that are interesting and engaging”
Latest inspection - comments:
“They make good progress during the Early Years – Children are provided with opportunities to explore learning through play”
Latest inspection - comments:
“There is an environment where children are encouraged to play with others and learn to share”
Latest inspection - comments:
“The school is a happy, positive place that pupils enjoy coming to”
Nursery Admissions
Visit our Nursery Admissions page or complete the form below to book your Nursery visit or request more information.
Book your Nursery Visit
“We are new to the school and I can’t tell you how much our child is flourishing at the Nursery. Best decision we ever made”
